Kevin Trudeau says most people only think about what they eat or drink, not what touches their skin.

His point: anything you put on your skin gets absorbed into your body, the same as food. Lotions, makeup, hair products, all of it.

His test: read the label. If it says to call poison control if ingested, ask why it's considered safe to rub on your skin every day instead.

He calls many of these ingredients hormone disruptors, interfering with how your body uses its own hormones.

Kevin Trudeau tells the story of Jack LaLanne, one of the longest-living figures from the early fitness era.

LaLanne's real supplement, Kevin says, wasn't a pill. It was desiccated beef liver. He didn't love the taste, so he mixed the powder into water and drank it down almost every day.

Kevin's point: the nutrients and B vitamins people chase in a bottle are already sitting in foods like liver and other organ meats, the ones almost nobody eats anymore.

His own rule: eat real, whole food as close to how nature made it, in season, and fermented the rest of the year.

Kevin Trudeau tells a story about scientists in Australia facing a bug problem. Their fix: import toads to eat the bugs.

It worked, the bugs disappeared. But the toads were poisonous, and the alligators that ate them died by the millions. With no alligators left, the rodents took over.

Kevin's point: nature runs on balance, and changing one piece of it can ripple out further than anyone planned.

His rule for food: whole, real food, as close to how nature made it, beats anything isolated or manufactured, like a gorilla eating a whole orange instead of drinking the juice.

Kevin Trudeau compares cleansing your body to changing the oil in your car.

His reasoning: you take your car in for an oil and filter change because things build up inside the engine. He says the same logic applies to your body. You shower to clean the outside, but the inside needs attention too.

His own habits: whole-food supplements made from real, dehydrated food instead of extracts, plus fasting and colon cleanses, to clear out what builds up.

His last word on it: the most important thing he does is take life lightly and laugh, because laughing is really the best medicine.
